claims.text: The proposed framework will separately calculate phonon and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Decoupling phonon and electronic transport will reduce lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction error by at least 30% relative to approaches that conflate the contributions.
A specimen containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen can be treated as defect-free or near-defect-free and low in impurities for purposes of the model.
Full phonon dispersion and scattering dynamics can be used to calculate the phonon contribution independently.
Independent evaluation of electronic structure can be used to calculate electronic thermal conductivity.
The method is applicable below 200 K, where experiments have separated lattice and electronic contributions.
The method is applicable from 300 to 1200 K, where total-conductivity data exist.
High sample purity is required so that defect scattering is minimized.
Atomic-scale complexity, including atomic-mass and force-constant variations, drives the temperature-dependent phonon dispersion.
Atomic-mass and force-constant variations drive the temperature-dependent electronic density of states.
The decoupled approach avoids reliance on a single Debye-temperature parameter.
The proposed phonon treatment captures details of phonon scattering that are inaccessible to analytical approaches.
Independent electronic modeling produces a clearer and less erroneous prediction of the lattice contribution.
Below 200 K, the predicted lattice conductivity will closely match the experimentally isolated lattice component.
From 300 to 1200 K, the separate lattice and electronic predictions will account for deviations in measured total conductivity.
Existing approaches generally combine lattice and electronic heat conduction into a single estimate and often depend on a Debye temperature.
Existing approaches have prediction errors exceeding 30% relative to experiment.
Significant impurity or defect scattering may cause the framework to break down.
There are insufficient high-temperature experimental data that independently isolate lattice and electronic conductivity.
Precise DFT modeling of complex vibrational spectra in high-entropy alloys remains challenging.

contradictions.description: The initial state treats approximately 1 wt.% oxygen as compatible with a defect-free or near-defect-free, low-impurity specimen, while the conditions and boundary require high purity and minimized impurity scattering without defining whether 1 wt.% oxygen satisfies that requirement.
